sections.text: Joshua Wong, a prominent pro-democracy activist, received a 10-year prison sentence in Hong Kong. He pleaded guilty to foreign collusion charges, specifically for conspiring to urge foreign powers to impose sanctions and blockades against China. gist: US voters rejected datacenter developments in numerous jurisdictions during recent midterm elections.
Bans and moratoriums were approved across multiple states, reflecting widespread anti-datacenter sentiment.
Analysts suggest the election results may slow the pace of future datacenter construction.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Voters in at least 40 jurisdictions across 10 states rejected datacenter developments during midterm elections. Municipalities in Ohio, Maine, and Kansas passed bans or moratoriums on these facilities. Only one location, Hardwood, North Dakota, voted against such restrictions. Additionally, candidates who opposed datacenter expansion were elected to office in states including Texas, Georgia, and Ohio.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Datacenters have become symbols of the tech industry and artificial intelligence. The election results demonstrate significant bipartisan opposition to these projects, which are viewed by some as resource-intensive. Analysts suggest this political shift creates hurdles for the tech sector and may lead to a slowdown in the development of new datacenter capacity.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Newly elected officials, such as Gina Hinojosa in Texas, have pledged to implement moratoriums and stricter regulations on construction. Industry observers anticipate that the political climate will create challenges for AI and tech legislation over the next two years.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A proposed study involving 14,000 newborns in Guinea-Bissau was cancelled after facing accusations of being unethical and neocolonial. The trial, funded by the US, planned to withhold a hepatitis B vaccine from half of the participants. Following public outcry and government intervention, the trial was prohibited, and police seized a batch of vaccines from the Bandim Health Project research centre.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The trial sparked international criticism because it withheld a vaccine recommended by the World Health Organization in a country where the infection is widespread. Experts argued that vulnerable populations were being exposed to risks that would not be accepted in wealthier nations. The controversy also highlighted tensions regarding research ethics and the influence of US vaccine policy.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Guinea-Bissau officials are considering introducing the birth-dose vaccine into the routine immunisation schedule earlier than the previously planned 2028 date. Meanwhile, police investigations into the seized vaccines and the circumstances surrounding the research centre continue.

sections.text: Iodine is essential for thyroid function, metabolism and brain development.
